hypotheses.text: Extraneural multi-system organ failure (hepatic cirrhosis, end-stage renal failure, diabetes mellitus, and pancytopenia) occurs in fewer than 10% of adult individuals with biallelic ACBD6 mutations and is restricted to specific familial backgrounds rather than representing an obligatory late-stage sequela in surviving adults.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifies whether the life-threatening visceral complications reported in Thai adult siblings by Yeetong et al. (2022) represent expected age-dependent natural history across the wider cohort of long-surviving adults (up to 50 years of age in Kaiyrzhanov et al., 2024) or an atypical isolated presentation influenced by secondary genetic or environmental factors.

evidence.text: Yeetong et al. reported two Thai adult siblings with homozygous ACBD6 c.360dup (p.Leu121Thrfs*27) who exhibited morbid obesity, pancytopenia with severe infections, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure leading to death in their early 30s, which had not been observed in earlier reported ACBD6 cases.

source.title: Neurodevelopmental Disorder, Obesity, Pancytopenia, Diabetes Mellitus, Cirrhosis, and Renal Failure in ACBD6-Associated Syndrome: A Case Report
source.quote: Clinical manifestations that have never been previously reported include morbid obesity, pancytopenia with severe infections, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, leading to deaths in their early 30s. Molecular studies identified a novel homozygous 1 base-pair duplication (c.360dup; p.Leu121Thrfs*27) in the ACBD6 gene.

age at death in affected siblings (years)

evidence.text: In an international cohort of 45 affected individuals aged 1 to 50 years harboring bi-allelic predominantly loss-of-function ACBD6 mutations, the clinical spectrum centered predominantly on progressive movement disorders, intellectual disability, cerebellar ataxia, and overweight (59%), without consistent reporting of cirrhosis, nephropathy, or pancytopenia across older adults.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The affected individuals (23 males and 22 females), aged 1-50 years, typically present with a complex and progressive disease involving moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) with significant expressive language impairment (98%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%) and mild cerebellar ataxia (85%) associated with gait impairment (94%), limb spasticity/hypertonia (76%), oculomotor (71%) and behavioural abnormalities (65%), overweight (59%), microcephaly (39%) and epilepsy (33%).

hypotheses.text: Metabolic dysregulation in ACBD6 deficiency frequently causes excessive weight gain/overweight (HP:0001513) in approximately 50-60% of patients across pediatric and adult cohorts, but does not autonomously progress to type 2 diabetes mellitus or diabetic nephropathy in the absence of secondary environmental or genetic co-factors.
hypotheses.rationale: Overweight is documented in 59% of patients across the 45-individual cohort, yet frank diabetes mellitus and renal failure have only been documented in the single sibship from Thailand, suggesting excessive adiposity alone does not inevitably trigger end-organ visceral failure.

evidence.text: Among 45 individuals with bi-allelic ACBD6 variants, overweight was documented in 59% (approx. 26/44), demonstrating high prevalence of metabolic adiposity across the broader disease cohort spanning ages 1 to 50 years.

evidence.text: Yeetong et al. noted that previous literature reported ACBD6 variants in patients with only neurological and craniofacial findings, whereas their two adult siblings showed morbid obesity alongside diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure.

source.quote: Biallelic variants in ACBD6 were previously reported in 7 patients with NDDs. Unfortunately, their clinical information remains very limited with descriptions of only their neurologic and craniofacial features.

hypotheses.text: Hematologic dysfunction (specifically refractory pancytopenia or severe recurring infections) is not a core manifestation of ACBD6 deficiency and does not manifest in non-consanguineous or diverse adult ACBD6 cohorts.
hypotheses.rationale: Pancytopenia is severe and lethal in the Yeetong et al. report, but no hematologic dysfunction was noted as a recurring phenotypic cardinal feature in the international multi-center study of 45 patients.

evidence.text: The international study of 45 individuals from 28 families detailing the core clinical syndrome of ACBD6 deficiency identified movement disorders, speech delay, ataxia, spasticity, facial dysmorphism, and structural midline brain anomalies without identifying cytopenias or bone marrow failure as recurring cardinal features.

new_directions.question_text: Did the adult ACBD6-deficient individuals aged >30 years in the Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2024) cohort undergo routine abdominal ultrasound, liver biochemistries, and complete blood counts, or were extraneural evaluations omitted due to focusing on the neurodevelopmental phenotype?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifies whether hepatic cirrhosis, nephropathy, and pancytopenia were truly absent or merely under-ascertained in the broader adult cohort.

new_directions.question_text: Could the homozygous c.360dup (p.Leu121Thrfs*27) variant or an adjacent linked homozygous variant unique to the consanguineous Thai pedigree explain the isolated multi-organ extraneural presentation?
new_directions.rationale: Determines whether homozygosity mapping in the Thai pedigree reveals contiguous gene defects or unmasked recessive alleles in another metabolic or hematologic locus.
